rules.statement: When adding a new heading to a Keep a Changelog section, make sure existing entries stay under the heading that fits them (Added, Changed, Fixed, …) rather than ending up under the inserted heading.
rules.why: If an entry lands under the wrong heading, the grouping breaks and the release notes misclassify the change, for example listing a version bump as a fix.
rules.check: In CHANGELOG.md diffs that insert a `### ` heading, look at the bullets that now sit below the new heading and confirm each one belongs to that category.

rules.statement: A test for a check that fails on one specific condition must assert evidence of that condition, such as the reported message, not just a non-zero exit code. Negative cases must assert that the evidence is absent.
rules.why: An exit-code-only assertion also passes when the check fails for some unrelated reason. The detection logic could then be deleted or broken while the suite stays green.
rules.check: Look for test cases that only compare an exit status when other cases expect the same status for different reasons. Check that they also assert the specific output.

rules.statement: In a test, don't discard a setup step's failure (for example with `|| true` or by ignoring its output and status). Assert that setup succeeded, so that only the behavior under test can cause the expected result.
rules.why: A swallowed setup failure can produce the outcome the test expects. That hides regressions and leaves fixtures unverified.
rules.check: Look for `|| true`, ignored return values, or suppressed output on fixture or setup commands in test scripts and test code.

rules.statement: When a wrapper or gate applies to several commands, its tests must exercise each wrapped command, not just one of them.
rules.why: A command the tests never exercise could stop being gated, and only a live CI run would reveal it.
rules.check: Compare the commands that CI or the docs route through the wrapper with the commands the wrapper's test cases actually invoke.

rules.statement: When CI starts running checks through a new script or a stricter gate, update the contributor docs' local-check instructions (AGENTS.md, README) to run them the same way. Say how the gate differs from the plain tool.
rules.why: Otherwise contributors run the plain tool locally, see it pass, and then CI fails on the stricter gate.
rules.check: In diffs that add a CI wrapper script or change how CI invokes a tool, check that AGENTS.md and README's local-check commands were updated to match.
